{"id": "000004e5-0000-4000-8000-0000000004e5", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_RDRb89lGMSZswhILow5oTa", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: serverless-operation-review\\\\ndescription: Operational review for AWS serverless workloads (Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, DynamoDB, and event sources SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Scheduler, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis) against the Well-Architected Serverless Applications Lens. Use when the user asks to review, audit, assess or health-check serverless functions or applications, or raises Lambda timeouts, throttling, concurrency, cold starts, memory sizing, missing dead-letter queues, events failing silently or dropped, poison-pill records, growing IteratorAge, duplicate SQS processing, deprecated runtimes, unauthenticated function URLs, or serverless cost and log-retention waste. Triggers \\'serverless review\\', \\'how healthy is my serverless workload\\', \\'audit the Lambda functions against best practices\\', \\'review my Lambda functions\\', \\'API Gateway review\\', \\'Step Functions review\\', \\'serverless ORR\\'. Load this skill before choosing subagent skills, and list it in preloaded_skills of every collection subagent.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  author: ankitsri-aws\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Reviews AWS serverless workloads \\\\u2014 Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, DynamoDB and Lambda event sources \\\\u2014 against the Well-Architected Serverless Applications Lens.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Serverless Operational Review\\\\n\\\\nConduct a structured operational review of an AWS serverless workload aligned with the\\\\n[AWS Well-Architected Framework](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/framework/welcome.html)\\\\nand the\\\\n[Serverless Applications Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/serverless-applications-lens/welcome.html),\\\\nthe [Lambda best practices guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/best-practices.html),\\\\nand the\\\\n[CloudWatch recommended alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Best_Practice_Recommended_Alarms_AWS_Services.html)\\\\nreference.\\\\n\\\\nThis skill uses **AWS Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, EventBridge,\\\\nEventBridge Scheduler, Kinesis, CloudWatch, CloudWatch Logs, IAM, and Cost Explorer read-only APIs\\\\nonly**. It never mutates a resource.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n\\\\nActivate this skill when the user asks to:\\\\n\\\\n- Review, audit, or assess serverless functions, APIs, state machines, or tables\\\\n- Check serverless best-practice compliance or run a serverless operational readiness review (ORR)\\\\n- Evaluate serverless reliability, performance, security, cost, or observability posture\\\\n- Diagnose recurring Lambda timeouts, throttles, OOM kills, cold starts, or silent event loss\\\\n- Understand why SQS messages are processed twice, why a stream is falling behind, or where\\\\n  asynchronous invocations are disappearing\\\\n- Find serverless cost waste (over-provisioned memory, x86 on Graviton-eligible runtimes, unbounded\\\\n  log retention, idle provisioned concurrency)\\\\n\\\\nDo **not** use this skill for container or database engine reviews. Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, Amazon\\\\nRDS/Aurora, Amazon Redshift, and Amazon MSK have their own dedicated review skills.\\\\n\\\\n## Review Scope Model\\\\n\\\\nFive resource families, any subset of which is a valid scope:\\\\n\\\\n| Family | Resources | Reviewed standalone? |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| Compute | Lambda functions, versions, aliases, function URLs | Yes |\\\\n| Event sources | SQS, SNS, EventBridge, EventBridge Scheduler, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis | Only as attached to a function |\\\\n| API | API Gateway REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs and their stages | Yes |\\\\n| Orchestration | Step Functions state machines | Yes |\\\\n| Data | DynamoDB tables and global secondary indexes | Yes |\\\\n\\\\n## Guardrails\\\\n\\\\nThese rules are non-negotiable and apply to every step.\\\\n\\\\n1. **Read-only.** Never call a mutating API. Recommend remediation; never apply it. If the user asks\\\\n   you to fix a finding, state the exact command or IaC change and let them run it.\\\\n2. **Never disclose secret material.** When reporting on environment variables, report the **key\\\\n   name only** \\\\u2014 never the value, and never a partial value. The same applies to anything found in\\\\n   logs that looks like a credential, token, connection string, or private key.\\\\n3. **Bound the work.** Follow the budget agreed in Step 1. Never sweep every region without being\\\\n   asked.\\\\n4. **Disclose what you skipped.** Every report states which regions were skipped, which resources\\\\n   were truncated by the budget, and which checks could not run for lack of permission.\\\\n5. **Never invent a threshold.** Every severity comes from the check catalogs in `references/`, each\\\\n   citing its AWS source. If a check has no documented threshold, report it as `INFO` and say the\\\\n   threshold is workload-specific. Name the source wherever you state a number, chat replies included.\\\\n6. **One reply carries the review.** The only text you may send starts with the heading\\\\n   `# Serverless health review: <region>` (shape in `references/delegation-and-output-shape.md`).\\\\n   Any other text, including \\\\\"still waiting\\\\\" on a subagent wake-up, is not sent. Outage: \\\\\"nothing checked\\\\\".\\\\n7. **A finding is a table row with a check id.** Columns: check id, severity, observed value, source\\\\n   API, doc or threshold source. An observation without a check id is context, not a finding.\\\\n8. **Keep three states apart.** Measured zero, no datapoints, and never queried are different results.\\\\n9. **Never print a 12-digit AWS account ID.** Use the alias or the last four digits.\\\\n\\\\nDelegating? Follow `references/delegation-and-output-shape.md` (prompt contents, wake-up rule).\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Review Checklist\\\\n\\\\nWork through these in order and track progress as you go. Each step depends on the output of the one\\\\nbefore it, and the detailed section for each carries the same step number.\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Establish scope and budget, and state both in the opening lines of the final reply\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Discover the serverless inventory, skipping empty Regions\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Collect configuration detail for the families in scope\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Collect 7-day CloudWatch metrics and compute the derived values\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: Collect and analyse logs, including the REPORT-line extraction\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: Assess alarm coverage against the Serverless Lens metric list\\\\n- [ ] Step 7: Analyse security posture and execution-role breadth\\\\n- [ ] Step 8: Analyse cost and quantify the savings opportunities\\\\n- [ ] Step 9: Evaluate everything collected against the check catalogs and assign severities\\\\n- [ ] Step 10: Generate the report, then run the pre-presentation checks\\\\n\\\\nSteps 4 through 8 are independent of each other once Step 3 is done, so collect them in whatever order\\\\nis convenient \\\\u2014 but do not start Step 9 until they have all either completed or been recorded as\\\\nskipped.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 1: Establish Scope and Budget\\\\n\\\\nAsk the user what to review. Accept any of:\\\\n\\\\n- Specific resource names or ARNs plus their Region (for example \\\\\"review the `checkout-processor`\\\\n  function in `eu-west-1`\\\\\")\\\\n- An application or stack boundary (a CloudFormation/SAM stack name, or a tag such as\\\\n  `Application=checkout`)\\\\n- All resources of a family in named Regions (\\\\\"all Lambda functions in us-east-1 and us-west-2\\\\\")\\\\n- All resources in all configured account Regions\\\\n\\\\nIf the user gives no scope, default to **all resource families in the caller\\'s current Region** and\\\\nsay so explicitly in the opening lines of the final reply.\\\\n\\\\n### Budget guardrail\\\\n\\\\nA wide serverless account can hold thousands of functions. Before collecting, state the plan and the\\\\ncap:\\\\n\\\\nDefault caps and the selection rule for each scope (named resources, stack or tag boundary,\\\\nnamed Regions, all Regions) are in `references/budget-and-cost-tables.md`. Read it before collecting.\\\\n\\\\nPut the budget in one line at the top of the final reply (not as a separate earlier message), for example:\\\\n\\\\n> Reviewing up to 25 Lambda functions, 10 API Gateway APIs, 10 state machines and 25 DynamoDB tables\\\\n> in `us-east-1`, selected by 7-day invocation volume. I will list anything I skip.\\\\n\\\\nIf the user asks for a bigger sweep, raise the cap \\\\u2014 but warn that a full multi-Region review of a\\\\nlarge account can take several hundred API calls and is best split by Region.\\\\n\\\\n**State the scope in the report.** Scope Covered lists the Regions, families, selection rule and caps\\\\napplied, even when the review finds nothing; \\\\\"no resources found\\\\\" means little without them.\\\\n\\\\n**Skip empty Regions.** Call the cheap list API first (`lambda:ListFunctions`,\\\\n`apigateway:GetRestApis`, `apigatewayv2:GetApis`, `states:ListStateMachines`,\\\\n`dynamodb:ListTables`); if a Region returns nothing for every family, record it as empty and move on\\\\nwithout further calls.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 2: Discover Serverless Inventory\\\\n\\\\nPer in-scope Region, enumerate the families in scope:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nlambda.ListFunctions                 # paginated; FunctionVersion=ALL only if versions are in scope\\\\nlambda.GetAccountSettings            # account concurrency quota + code storage (once per Region)\\\\napigateway.GetRestApis               # REST APIs\\\\napigatewayv2.GetApis                 # HTTP + WebSocket APIs\\\\nstates.ListStateMachines             # state machines\\\\ndynamodb.ListTables                  # tables\\\\nlambda.ListEventSourceMappings       # paginated; maps functions to SQS/streams/MSK/Kafka\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nWrite the counts in your working notes before any deep collection, then pick the mode. Collect\\\\ninline unless a count exceeds 40 functions or 25 of another family; see\\\\n`references/delegation-and-output-shape.md` section 1. Do not call `subagent` before this line exists:\\\\n\\\\n`inventory: functions=N tables=N apis=N machines=N mappings=N -> mode: inline | delegate(<why>)`\\\\n\\\\nThe inventory table goes in the final reply, in this shape:\\\\n\\\\n| Type | Name | Region | Runtime / Protocol / Type | Key attribute |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| Lambda | `checkout-processor` | us-east-1 | python3.13, arm64 | 1024 MB / 30 s |\\\\n| API (HTTP) | `checkout-api` | us-east-1 | HTTP | 2 stages |\\\\n| State machine | `order-saga` | us-east-1 | STANDARD | logging OFF |\\\\n| Table | `orders` | us-east-1 | PAY_PER_REQUEST | PITR off |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 3: Collect Configuration Detail\\\\n\\\\nCollect per resource, for the families in scope. `references/collection-reference.md` lists the exact\\\\nAPI calls and the fields each one contributes to a check \\\\u2014 use it rather than improvising a call list,\\\\nbecause a field you skip is a check that silently cannot fire.\\\\n\\\\n| Family | Primary calls |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| Lambda | `GetFunctionConfiguration`, `GetFunctionConcurrency`, `GetFunctionEventInvokeConfig`, `ListProvisionedConcurrencyConfigs`, `ListAliases`, `ListFunctionUrlConfigs`, `GetPolicy`, `ListTags` |\\\\n| Event sources | `sqs.GetQueueAttributes` (with `AttributeNames=All`), `sns.GetSubscriptionAttributes`, `events.ListTargetsByRule`, `scheduler.GetSchedule`, `kinesis.DescribeStreamSummary`, plus the event source mapping fields |\\\\n| API Gateway | `apigateway.GetStages`/`GetMethod`/`GetAuthorizers`/`GetUsagePlans`, `apigatewayv2.GetStages`/`GetRoutes`, `wafv2.GetWebACLForResource` |\\\\n| Step Functions | `states.DescribeStateMachine` (parse the ASL definition), `states.ListExecutions` |\\\\n| DynamoDB | `dynamodb.DescribeTable`, `DescribeContinuousBackups`, `DescribeTimeToLive`, `application-autoscaling.DescribeScalableTargets` |\\\\n\\\\nThe single most important cross-check in this step: **an SQS queue\\'s `VisibilityTimeout` against the\\\\nconsuming function\\'s `Timeout`**. A queue timeout below the function timeout produces duplicate\\\\nprocessing and is a CRITICAL finding \\\\u2014 see `references/checks-event-sources.md`.\\\\n\\\\nReport environment variables by **key name only**. Never the value.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 4: Collect CloudWatch Metrics (7-Day)\\\\n\\\\nMake **one** `cloudwatch.GetMetricData` call per resource. `Period: 21600` (6 hours).\\\\n`StartTime`: 7 days ago. `EndTime`: now. Percentiles require `ExtendedStatistic`, not `Statistic`.\\\\n\\\\n`references/metrics-and-logs.md` lists the exact metric set per resource type \\\\u2014 Lambda (per function\\\\nand account level), SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Scheduler, Kinesis, API Gateway, Step Functions, and\\\\nDynamoDB \\\\u2014 as `| id | metricName | stat | unit |` tables. Use it rather than improvising a metric\\\\nlist, so reports stay comparable between runs.\\\\n\\\\nA metric that returns no data because the configuration does not emit it is not a finding. Omit the\\\\nrow.\\\\n\\\\n### Derived values\\\\n\\\\nCompute these once and reuse them in Steps 6, 9, and 10:\\\\n\\\\n| Derived value | Formula | Used by |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| Error rate | `Errors / Invocations` over the window | reliability findings |\\\\n| Throttle rate | `Throttles / (Invocations + Throttles)` | scaling findings |\\\\n| Timeout headroom | `Duration p99 / (Timeout \\\\u00d7 1000)` | performance findings |\\\\n| Concurrency headroom | `ClaimedAccountConcurrency / AccountLimit.ConcurrentExecutions` | scaling findings |\\\\n| Memory utilization | `Max Memory Used / MemorySize` (from Step 5) | cost and performance findings |\\\\n| PC utilization | `ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization` with `...SpilloverInvocations` | cost findings |\\\\n| Invocation cost weight | `Invocations \\\\u00d7 Duration(avg) \\\\u00d7 MemorySize` | cost split in Step 8 |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 5: Collect and Analyze Logs\\\\n\\\\nPer function, resolve the log group (`LoggingConfig.LogGroup`, default `/aws/lambda/<name>`) then:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nlogs.DescribeLogGroups   # logGroupNamePrefix; capture retentionInDays and storedBytes\\\\nlogs.FilterLogEvents     # 7-day window, one call per pattern, limit results\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nA log group that does not exist means the function has never been invoked \\\\u2014 report `INFO`, not a\\\\nfailure.\\\\n\\\\nTwo things to extract:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Error patterns** \\\\u2014 `references/metrics-and-logs.md` carries the pattern table (timeouts, OOM\\\\n   kills, import failures, ENI exhaustion, downstream throttling, permission denials, recursive-loop\\\\n   detection, socket timeouts). Record occurrence counts plus first and last occurrence for anything\\\\n   above zero.\\\\n2. **Memory and cold starts** \\\\u2014 every invocation emits a `REPORT` line carrying `Max Memory Used`,\\\\n   `Memory Size`, `Init Duration`, and `Billed Duration`. Parse **both** the text and JSON log\\\\n   formats; `LogFormat: JSON` moves these into `record.metrics`. Sample 200\\\\u2013500 REPORT lines across\\\\n   the window rather than scanning exhaustively, and state the sample size in the report.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 6: Assess Alarm Coverage\\\\n\\\\nFor each in-scope resource, call `cloudwatch.DescribeAlarmsForMetric` for the metrics the Serverless\\\\nApplications Lens names for that service. A missing alarm is a `MEDIUM` finding, and every reported\\\\ngap must carry the recommended statistic, threshold, period, and datapoints-to-alarm so the gap list\\\\ndoubles as an implementation plan.\\\\n\\\\nThe authoritative per-service list, with the recommended alarm settings, is in\\\\n`references/cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md`. Per-service metric lists are in that file.\\\\n\\\\nAlso assess the wider observability posture: `TracingConfig.Mode` on functions, `tracingEnabled` on\\\\nAPI stages and state machines, `LogFormat` (text logging is a `LOW` finding \\\\u2014 the Lens asks for\\\\nstructured JSON logging), and whether alarms exist at both the individual resource level and an\\\\naggregate level.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 7: Security and IAM Analysis\\\\n\\\\n### 7.1 Runtime currency\\\\n\\\\nCompare each function\\'s `Runtime` against `references/lambda-runtime-deprecations.md`. Never guess a\\\\ndeprecation date \\\\u2014 if the runtime is absent from the table, say the date is unverified and link the\\\\n[runtime support policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtimes.html).\\\\n\\\\n### 7.2 Execution role breadth\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\niam.GetRole\\\\niam.ListAttachedRolePolicies      # then iam.GetPolicy + iam.GetPolicyVersion per ARN\\\\niam.ListRolePolicies              # then iam.GetRolePolicy per inline policy\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nFlag: `AdministratorAccess` or any `\\\\\"Action\\\\\": \\\\\"*\\\\\"` with `\\\\\"Resource\\\\\": \\\\\"*\\\\\"` (CRITICAL), service-level\\\\nwildcards such as `s3:*` or `dynamodb:*` (HIGH), `iam:PassRole` with `Resource: \\\\\"*\\\\\"` (HIGH), and a\\\\ntrust policy that allows a principal other than `lambda.amazonaws.com` without a condition (HIGH).\\\\n\\\\n**Summarise the policy; do not reproduce it.** Report the policy name and the specific offending\\\\nactions and resources as a short list \\\\u2014 for example \\\\\"inline policy `far-too-broad` grants\\\\n`dynamodb:*`, `sqs:*`, `sns:*` on `Resource: \\\\\"*\\\\\"`\\\\\". Do not paste the full policy JSON into the\\\\nreport. Beyond keeping the finding readable, verbatim policy documents have been observed to trip\\\\nthe agent\\'s content safety filter, which aborts the response mid-review and loses the whole report.\\\\n\\\\n### 7.3 Invocation exposure\\\\n\\\\n- `lambda.GetPolicy` \\\\u2014 a statement with `\\\\\"Principal\\\\\": \\\\\"*\\\\\"` or `\\\\\"Principal\\\\\": {\\\\\"AWS\\\\\": \\\\\"*\\\\\"}` and no\\\\n  `SourceArn`/`SourceAccount` condition is CRITICAL\\\\n- `lambda.GetFunctionUrlConfig` \\\\u2014 `AuthType: NONE` is a public, unauthenticated HTTPS entry point.\\\\n  CRITICAL unless the user confirms it is intentionally public, in which case HIGH with a note to\\\\n  front it with CloudFront and WAF\\\\n- API Gateway stages with no authorizer and no API key and no WAF association \\\\u2014 HIGH\\\\n- `disableExecuteApiEndpoint: false` on an API that is only meant to be reached through a custom\\\\n  domain \\\\u2014 MEDIUM\\\\n\\\\n### 7.4 Data protection\\\\n\\\\n- Environment variables with no `KMSKeyArn` (Lambda-managed key only) \\\\u2014 MEDIUM when a key name\\\\n  suggests secret material. **Report key names only.** Recommend AWS Secrets Manager or SSM\\\\n  Parameter Store rather than environment variables for secrets\\\\n- Key-name heuristics that warrant the finding: `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `SECRET`, `TOKEN`, `API_KEY`,\\\\n  `APIKEY`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `CREDENTIAL`, `CONNECTION_STRING`, `DSN`, `AUTH`\\\\n- SQS queues and SNS topics without `KmsMasterKeyId` \\\\u2014 MEDIUM\\\\n- DynamoDB tables without a customer-managed key, where the workload handles regulated data \\\\u2014 LOW\\\\n  (AWS-owned key encryption is on by default)\\\\n- Functions with no `CodeSigningConfigArn` \\\\u2014 LOW\\\\n\\\\nIf a log-pattern scan surfaces what looks like a credential in a log line, report **that it happened\\\\nand in which log group**, never the value, and raise it as HIGH.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 8: Cost Analysis\\\\n\\\\nOnce per review, not per resource:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\ncostexplorer.GetCostAndUsage    # 3 months, MONTHLY, GroupBy USAGE_TYPE,\\\\n                                #   Filter Service IN [\\\\\"AWS Lambda\\\\\", \\\\\"AmazonCloudWatch\\\\\",\\\\n                                #   \\\\\"Amazon API Gateway\\\\\", \\\\\"Amazon DynamoDB\\\\\", \\\\\"AWS Step Functions\\\\\"]\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nCost Explorer does not break Lambda spend down per function. Estimate a per-function share and label\\\\nit clearly:\\\\n\\\\n1. Take the most recent full month\\'s Lambda spend.\\\\n2. Weight each function by `Invocations \\\\u00d7 Duration(avg) \\\\u00d7 MemorySize` from Step 4.\\\\n3. Split the month total across functions by weight.\\\\n4. Mark every derived figure **(estimated)** in the report.\\\\n\\\\nQuantify these opportunities, each with its own finding. The signal and typical saving for each are in\\\\n`references/budget-and-cost-tables.md`. They are: memory rightsizing, Graviton migration, log retention, log volume, idle provisioned concurrency,\\\\nunused functions, DynamoDB capacity mode, and Step Functions type.\\\\n\\\\nAlways state that memory changes should be validated with\\\\n[AWS Lambda Power Tuning](https://github.com/alexcasalboni/aws-lambda-power-tuning) rather than\\\\napplied blind, because reducing memory also reduces CPU.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 9: Evaluate Against Best Practices\\\\n\\\\nEvaluate every collected value against the check catalogs, and assign exactly one severity per\\\\nfinding:\\\\n\\\\n| Catalog | Covers |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| `references/checks-lambda.md` | function configuration, concurrency, performance, security, cost |\\\\n| `references/checks-event-sources.md` | SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Scheduler, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis |\\\\n| `references/checks-apigateway.md` | REST, HTTP, WebSocket APIs and stages |\\\\n| `references/checks-stepfunctions.md` | state machines and ASL definitions |\\\\n| `references/checks-dynamodb.md` | tables, GSIs, backups, capacity |\\\\n| `references/cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md` | alarm coverage and recommended alarm settings |\\\\n| `references/api-quirks.md` | API responses whose obvious reading is wrong |\\\\n| `references/collection-reference.md` | the API calls and fields to collect per resource family |\\\\n| `references/metrics-and-logs.md` | the metric set per resource type and the log pattern table |\\\\n| `references/lambda-runtime-deprecations.md` | runtime end-of-support dates |\\\\n| `references/delegation-and-output-shape.md` | finding table, delegation prompt, three result states, outage reply |\\\\n\\\\nEach catalog row carries a check id, pillar, severity, detection rule, remediation, and its AWS\\\\ndocumentation citation. Use the catalog severity as-is.\\\\n\\\\n**Quote the check id in every finding you report**, wherever that finding appears \\\\u2014 the report\\\\nartifact, a chat reply, a one-line summary. \\\\\"SLS-SQS-002\\\\\" lets the reader look up the detection rule\\\\nand its AWS source, and lets two runs be compared line by line; a finding without it is not traceable\\\\nand is not acceptable output. Adjust the catalog severity only for stated context and say so in the\\\\nfinding \\\\u2014 a public function URL the user has confirmed is a public webhook drops from CRITICAL to HIGH.\\\\n\\\\nGroup findings by Well-Architected pillar for the report: Security, Reliability, Performance\\\\nEfficiency, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Step 10: Generate Report\\\\n\\\\nUse the structure in `references/report-template.md`.\\\\n\\\\n**Artifact naming and granularity:**\\\\n\\\\n- Targeted review of one to three named resources \\\\u2014 one artifact per resource, named\\\\n  `serverless-review-<resource-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`\\\\n- Anything wider (stack, tag, Region, account) \\\\u2014 a single consolidated artifact named\\\\n  `serverless-review-<scope-label>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` with a per-resource section inside\\\\n\\\\nSection order, which matches the other operation-review skills in this repository:\\\\n\\\\n1. Report Header\\\\n2. Executive Summary \\\\u2014 health verdict, finding counts by severity, top 3 critical/high items\\\\n3. Scope Covered \\\\u2014 Regions reviewed, Regions skipped as empty, resources truncated by budget, checks\\\\n   skipped for missing permissions\\\\n4. Configuration Snapshot\\\\n5. Findings by Pillar \\\\u2014 Security, Reliability, Performance, Cost, Operational Excellence\\\\n6. CloudWatch Metrics (7-Day)\\\\n7. Log Pattern Analysis\\\\n8. Alarm Coverage\\\\n9. Cost Summary\\\\n10. Priority Matrix\\\\n11. Next Steps \\\\u2014 Immediate / Short-term / Long-term, per the severity SLAs\\\\n12. Appendix \\\\u2014 reference links\\\\n\\\\nEvery finding must carry: what was observed (with the concrete value), why it matters, the\\\\nrecommendation, and a remediation snippet (AWS CLI, SAM/CloudFormation, or CDK). Never present a\\\\nfinding without evidence.\\\\n\\\\n### Before you present anything \\\\u2014 check your own output\\\\n\\\\nA review that is confidently wrong is worse than one that admits a gap. Run this list against the\\\\nreport, and equally against the answer you type in chat, and fix what fails before presenting either:\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] **Evidence on every finding.** Each one names the observed value, not just the conclusion. If a\\\\n      finding says \\\\\"no DLQ configured\\\\\" without naming the absent fields, add them.\\\\n- [ ] **Severities match the catalogs.** Re-read the check id you assigned. If you adjusted a severity\\\\n      for context, the finding says so and says why.\\\\n- [ ] **No invented thresholds.** Every numeric threshold traces to a catalog row. Where AWS publishes\\\\n      none, the finding says the threshold is workload-specific.\\\\n- [ ] **Absent metrics are not findings.** A metric with no datapoints because the configuration does\\\\n      not emit it was omitted, not reported as a failure.\\\\n- [ ] **Cost figures are marked (estimated)** and the split method is stated. No estimate is presented\\\\n      as a bill.\\\\n- [ ] **No secret values anywhere.** Environment variables appear by key name only. Nothing\\\\n      credential-shaped from a log line was reproduced.\\\\n- [ ] **Scope Covered is complete.** Every Region skipped, resource truncated, and check that could not\\\\n      run is listed \\\\u2014 including the ones denied by permission or platform restriction.\\\\n- [ ] **Counts reconcile.** The severity counts in the Executive Summary equal the findings in the body.\\\\n- [ ] **The verdict follows the rule.** Any CRITICAL means \\\\u274c; otherwise any HIGH means \\\\u26a0\\\\ufe0f; otherwise \\\\u2705.\\\\n\\\\nIf a check in this list cannot be satisfied, say so where you present the findings rather than\\\\nquietly dropping it.\\\\n\\\\n### When the answer is a chat reply\\\\n\\\\nThe report often goes to an artifact while the user reads only what you type back. That reply is the\\\\nreview in short form, and every rule above holds in it unchanged: each finding keeps its check id,\\\\nobserved value, severity and recommendation, and each threshold keeps its source. Use the finding\\\\ntable in `references/delegation-and-output-shape.md`. Drop whole findings to fit a length, never a\\\\nfinding\\'s attributes, and never claim check ids you did not print.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Severity Definitions\\\\n\\\\n| Severity | Definition | SLA |\\\\n|----------|------------|-----|\\\\n| CRITICAL | Immediate risk to availability, security, or data integrity | Fix within 24\\\\u201348 hours |\\\\n| HIGH | Significant gap that could lead to incidents | Fix within 1 week |\\\\n| MEDIUM | Notable improvement opportunity | Plan within 30 days |\\\\n| LOW | Minor optimization or hardening | Address when convenient |\\\\n| INFO | Observation, no action required | N/A |\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling and API Quirks\\\\n\\\\n`references/api-quirks.md` carries the error table and the API responses whose obvious reading is\\\\nwrong. Read it before interpreting a response as a finding. An `AccessDeniedException` never silently\\\\ndisappears: skip that check, record the missing action, and report it in Scope Covered. The two quirks\\\\nthat most often cause a false finding:\\\\n\\\\n- `lambda.GetFunctionEventInvokeConfig` raising `ResourceNotFoundException` means **defaults apply**\\\\n  (2 retries, 6-hour maximum event age, no destination), not that something is broken.\\\\n- `lambda.GetFunctionConcurrency` returning empty means the function is **unreserved**. Repeated errors block processing of the affected\\n  shard until the error is resolved or the items expire.\"\\n  ([Lens \u2014 Failure management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/serverless-applications-lens/failure-management.html))\\n- The Lens names four controls for stream resilience: **Maximum Retry Attempts**, **Maximum Record\\n  Age**, **Destination on Failure**, and **Bisect Batch on Function Error**.\\n- Lambda best practices recommends alarming on stream `IteratorAge`, with an example threshold of\\n  30,000 ms.\\n- CloudWatch notes that if iterator age passes 50% of the stream retention period there is a risk of\\n  data loss through record expiry.\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-STR-001 | REL | CRITICAL | Mapping has none of `MaximumRetryAttempts`, `MaximumRecordAgeInSeconds`, `BisectBatchOnFunctionError`, or `DestinationConfig.OnFailure` | A single poison-pill record blocks the shard until the records expire. As an immediate mitigation raise the retention period while the consumer is fixed | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds`: \"If an iterator\\'s age passes 50% of the retention period\u2026 there is a risk for data loss\" |\\n| SLS-STR-008 | REL | HIGH | `IteratorAge` sustained above 30,000 ms (or a workload-specific target) | The consumer is falling behind. The handler must inspect the response and deal with partial failures programmatically | Lens \u2014 Failure management: \"Always inspect the response when using such operations\" |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Cross-cutting event source checks\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-ESM-001 | REL | HIGH | A function has an event source mapping whose `State` is `Disabled`, and the source is still receiving traffic | The source is accumulating a backlog with no consumer | Lambda event source mappings |\\n| SLS-ESM-002 | REL | MEDIUM | `LastProcessingResult` on the mapping reports a persistent error (for example `PROBLEM: Function call failed`) | Read the mapping\\'s last processing result before assuming the function itself is healthy | Lambda event source mappings |\\n| SLS-ESM-003 | REL | LOW | Filter criteria are absent on a high-volume source where the handler immediately discards most events | Move the filter into the event source mapping so Lambda is not invoked for events it will drop | Lambda event filtering |\\n| SLS-ESM-004 | OPS | LOW | `MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds` is 0 on a low-traffic queue or stream | A batching window reduces invocation count on sparse traffic. Note that with a batch window on a low-traffic SQS queue Lambda may wait up to 20 seconds before invoking | Lambda batching behaviour |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Remediation snippets\\n\\n### Correct an SQS visibility timeout\\n\\n```bash\\n# Recommended: 6 x function timeout, plus the batch window when one is configured.\\n# Example: 30 s function timeout, 0 s batch window -> 180 s\\naws sqs set-queue-attributes \\\\\\n  --queue-url https://sqs.REGION.amazonaws.com/ACCOUNT/orders \\\\\\n  --attributes VisibilityTimeout=180\\n```\\n\\n### Attach a dead-letter queue with a sensible receive count\\n\\n```yaml\\nResources:\\n  OrdersQueue:\\n    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue\\n    Properties:\\n      VisibilityTimeout: 180\\n      RedrivePolicy:\\n        deadLetterTargetArn: !GetAtt OrdersDLQ.Arn\\n        maxReceiveCount: 5\\n  OrdersDLQ:\\n    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue\\n    Properties:\\n      MessageRetentionPeriod: 1209600   # 14 days, the maximum\\n```\\n\\n### Enable partial batch response\\n\\n```bash\\naws lambda update-event-source-mapping \\\\\\n  --uuid a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-EXAMPLE11111 \\\\\\n  --function-response-types ReportBatchItemFailures\\n```\\n\\nThe handler must also return the failed message identifiers:\\n\\n```json\\n{ \"batchItemFailures\": [ { \"itemIdentifier\": \"0000003e-0000-4000-8000-00000000003e\" } ] }\\n```\\n\\n### Harden a stream event source mapping\\n\\n```bash\\naws lambda update-event-source-mapping \\\\\\n  --uuid a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-EXAMPLE11111 \\\\\\n  --maximum-retry-attempts 5 \\\\\\n  --maximum-record-age-in-seconds 3600 \\\\\\n  --bisect-batch-on-function-error \\\\\\n  --function-response-types ReportBatchItemFailures \\\\\\n  --destination-config \\'{\"OnFailure\":{\"Destination\":\"arn:aws:sqs:REGION:ACCOUNT:stream-failures\"}}\\'\\n```\\n\\n### Add a DLQ to an EventBridge rule target\\n\\n```yaml\\nTargets:\\n  - Id: ProcessOrder\\n    Arn: !GetAtt OrderProcessor.Arn\\n    DeadLetterConfig:\\n      Arn: !GetAtt EventBridgeDLQ.Arn\\n    RetryPolicy:\\n      MaximumRetryAttempts: 10\\n      MaximumEventAgeInSeconds: 3600\\n```\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_ARJAv0oRRnKDmMIfRdyC8A", "content": "[{'text': '# Check Catalog \u2014 Amazon API Gateway\\n\\nCovers REST APIs (`apigateway`), HTTP APIs and WebSocket APIs (`apigatewayv2`), and their stages.\\n\\nPillar codes: **SEC** Security \u00b7 **REL** Reliability \u00b7 **PERF** Performance Efficiency \u00b7\\n**COST** Cost Optimization \u00b7 **OPS** Operational Excellence\\n\\nCapability differences that change what counts as a finding \u2014 do not report a missing feature that\\nthe API type does not support:\\n\\n| Capability | REST | HTTP | WebSocket |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| Response caching | Yes | No | No |\\n| AWS WAF association | Yes | No | No |\\n| Usage plans and API keys | Yes | No | No |\\n| Request/response validation | Yes | Limited | No |\\n| Access logging | Yes | Yes | Yes |\\n| Execution logging with `dataTraceEnabled` | Yes | Route-level settings | Yes |\\n| X-Ray tracing | Yes | No | No |\\n| mTLS (requires a custom domain) | Yes | Yes | No |\\n\\nDocumented thresholds used below, from\\n[CloudWatch recommended alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Best_Practice_Recommended_Alarms_AWS_Services.html):\\n4XX and 5XX error **ratio** 0.05 (5% of requests), `Latency` p90 2500 ms, `IntegrationLatency`\\np90 2000 ms.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Security\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-APG-001 | SEC | HIGH | A route or method has `authorizationType: NONE`, no `apiKeyRequired`, and the stage has no WAF association | The endpoint is open to the internet. Add a Lambda authorizer, IAM auth, a JWT authorizer (HTTP APIs), or a Cognito user pool authorizer. Drops to MEDIUM only when the user confirms the route is intentionally public, in which case require WAF plus stage throttling | API Gateway control access |\\n| SLS-APG-002 | SEC | MEDIUM | REST stage with no AWS WAF web ACL association on a public API | WAF gives managed rule protection against common exploits and rate-based blocking. Note HTTP APIs cannot associate a WAF web ACL \u2014 for those, front the API with CloudFront | AWS WAF with API Gateway |\\n| SLS-APG-003 | SEC | MEDIUM | `disableExecuteApiEndpoint` is `false` on an API that is reached through a custom domain | The default `execute-api` endpoint stays reachable and bypasses the custom domain\\'s controls. Disable it | API Gateway custom domains |\\n| SLS-APG-004 | SEC | MEDIUM | REST API uses API keys as the only access control | API keys identify a caller for metering; they are not an authentication mechanism. Add a real authorizer | API Gateway usage plans and API keys |\\n| SLS-APG-005 | SEC | HIGH | `methodSettings` has `dataTraceEnabled: true` on a production stage | Full request and response bodies are written to CloudWatch Logs, which can capture credentials and personal data. Disable it outside of active debugging | API Gateway CloudWatch logging |\\n| SLS-APG-006 | SEC | LOW | Custom domain with no `mutualTlsAuthentication` on a machine-to-machine API where client identity matters | mTLS authenticates the client certificate at the edge | API Gateway mutual TLS |\\n| SLS-APG-007 | SEC | LOW | Custom domain `securityPolicy` is not `TLS_1_2` or later | Raise the minimum TLS version | API Gateway custom domain security policy |\\n| SLS-APG-008 | SEC | MEDIUM | REST stage with `cachingEnabled: true` and `cacheDataEncrypted: false` | Encrypt cached responses, which may contain authorised data for another caller | API Gateway caching |\\n| SLS-APG-009 | SEC | MEDIUM | REST API with no request validation on methods that accept a body | Validate at the edge so malformed payloads never reach the integration and never bill an invocation | API Gateway request validation |\\n| SLS-APG-010 | SEC | LOW | Private REST API (`PRIVATE` endpoint type) with a resource policy that does not restrict the source VPC endpoint | Scope the resource policy to the intended `aws:SourceVpce` | API Gateway private APIs |\\n\\n## Reliability and scaling\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-APG-020 | REL | HIGH | 5XX error ratio \u2265 5% of requests | Something is wrong in the backend, the network, or the integration. Correlate with the integration\\'s own error metric | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `5XXError`/`5xx`, threshold 0.05 |\\n| SLS-APG-021 | REL | MEDIUM | 4XX error ratio \u2265 5% of requests | Usually authorization or request-shape problems, but also the signature of throttling (HTTP 429). Check for 429s specifically before assuming client error | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `4XXError`/`4xx`, threshold 0.05 |\\n| SLS-APG-022 | REL | HIGH | Stage has no `throttlingRateLimit`/`throttlingBurstLimit` (inherits only the account limit) | Without stage or method throttling, one caller can consume the account\\'s entire request rate and starve every other API. Set a stage-level limit sized to the expected load | Lens \u2014 Limits: \"API Gateway and Lambda have different limits for steady and burst request rates\" |\\n| SLS-APG-023 | REL | MEDIUM | Integration timeout is set at or near the API type\\'s maximum while the backing Lambda function\\'s `Timeout` is longer | The client receives a 504 while the function keeps running and billing. Align the two. Read the account\\'s applied `Maximum integration timeout` quota with `service-quotas get-service-quota` rather than assuming the default | API Gateway quotas |\\n| SLS-APG-024 | REL | MEDIUM | No usage plan on a REST API exposed to third parties | Usage plans give per-consumer throttling and quotas, which protects the backend from a single misbehaving client | API Gateway usage plans |\\n| SLS-APG-025 | REL | LOW | Single-Region API with no Route 53 failover or multi-Region deployment, for a workload with a stated Regional resilience requirement | Note the gap against the requirement rather than prescribing multi-Region unconditionally | Well-Architected REL |\\n| SLS-APG-026 | REL | MEDIUM | WebSocket API with `ExecutionError` > 0 | Integration invocation is failing \u2014 5xx from the integration, permissions, throttling, or a deleted target | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `ExecutionError`, threshold 0.05 |\\n| SLS-APG-027 | REL | MEDIUM | WebSocket API with `ClientError` > 0 above 5% | Authorization or message-shape problems, or a route that no longer exists | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `ClientError`, threshold 0.05 |\\n| SLS-APG-028 | REL | INFO | `Count` drops far below the established baseline on an API with predictable traffic | Can indicate clients calling the wrong endpoint, or a permissions or configuration change making the API unreachable | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `Count`, `LESS_THAN_THRESHOLD` |\\n\\n## Performance efficiency\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-APG-040 | PERF | HIGH | `Latency` p90 \u2265 2500 ms | Compare with `IntegrationLatency`: if the two track each other the backend is the cause; if `Latency` is materially higher, the overhead is in API Gateway (authorizer, validation, mapping templates) | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `Latency` p90, threshold 2500 ms |\\n| SLS-APG-041 | PERF | MEDIUM | `IntegrationLatency` p90 \u2265 2000 ms | The backend is slow. For Lambda integrations correlate with the function\\'s `Duration` and cold-start rate | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 `IntegrationLatency` p90, threshold 2000 ms |\\n| SLS-APG-042 | PERF | LOW | REST stage with caching disabled on read-heavy, cacheable endpoints | Caching cuts both latency and backend cost. Only applies to REST APIs | API Gateway caching |\\n| SLS-APG-043 | PERF | LOW | REST stage cache hit ratio (`CacheHitCount / (CacheHitCount + CacheMissCount)`) below 50% | The cache is being paid for without benefit. Review the cache key and TTL, or turn it off | API Gateway caching |\\n| SLS-APG-044 | PERF | LOW | REST API with no `minimumCompressionSize` on endpoints returning large payloads | Compression reduces transfer time and data-out cost | API Gateway payload compression |\\n| SLS-APG-045 | PERF | LOW | `EDGE` endpoint type where all clients are in one Region, or `REGIONAL` where clients are global and no CloudFront distribution fronts the API | Match the endpoint type to the client distribution | API Gateway endpoint types |\\n\\n## Operational excellence\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-APG-060 | OPS | HIGH | Stage has no `accessLogSettings` | Without access logs there is no per-request record for incident reconstruction. Enable access logging to CloudWatch Logs or Firehose with a structured format | Lens \u2014 Centralized and structured logging |\\n| SLS-APG-061 | OPS | MEDIUM | `methodSettings` `loggingLevel` is `OFF` | Set `ERROR` at minimum so failures are explainable. `INFO` for debugging only | API Gateway CloudWatch logging |\\n| SLS-APG-062 | OPS | MEDIUM | REST stage with `tracingEnabled: false` | Enable X-Ray so latency can be attributed across the API, the function, and its downstreams. Not available for HTTP APIs | Lens \u2014 Distributed tracing |\\n| SLS-APG-063 | OPS | MEDIUM | No alarm on `5XXError` | See `cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md` | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts (alert on `5XXError`) |\\n| SLS-APG-064 | OPS | MEDIUM | No alarm on `Latency` | as above | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts (alert on `Latency`) |\\n| SLS-APG-065 | OPS | MEDIUM | No alarm on `IntegrationLatency` | as above | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts (alert on `IntegrationLatency`) |\\n| SLS-APG-066 | OPS | MEDIUM | WebSocket API with no alarm on `ClientError`, `IntegrationError`, or `ExecutionError` | as above | Lens \u2014 Metrics and alerts: \"For WebSocket API, use `ClientError`, `IntegrationError` and `ExecutionError`\" |\\n| SLS-APG-067 | OPS | LOW | Detailed CloudWatch metrics disabled on a stage with multiple resources or routes | Without detailed metrics, errors and latency cannot be attributed to a specific method or route | CloudWatch recommended alarms \u2014 repeatedly recommends enabling detailed metrics to narrow the source |\\n| SLS-APG-068 | OPS | LOW | No stage variables or separate stages for environments; a single stage serves multiple environments | Separate stages per environment so throttling, logging, and integrations can differ | API Gateway stages |\\n| SLS-APG-069 | OPS | LOW | Missing operational tags \u2014 `Environment`, `Owner`, `Runbook`, `OnCall` | Tag for ownership routing and cost allocation | Well-Architected OPS |\\n\\n## Cost optimization\\n\\n| ID | Pillar | Severity | Detection | Remediation | Source |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| SLS-APG-080 | COST | MEDIUM | REST API used for a simple proxy integration with no REST-only features (caching, usage plans, request validation, WAF, X-Ray) | HTTP APIs cost materially less per request. Migrating is a real saving when none of the REST-only features are in use | API Gateway pricing; choosing between REST and HTTP APIs |\\n| SLS-APG-081 | COST | MEDIUM | REST cache enabled with a low hit ratio | The cache cluster is billed hourly by size regardless of hits | API Gateway caching pricing |\\n| SLS-APG-082 | COST | LOW | Access logs or execution logs with `dataTraceEnabled` writing to a log group with no retention policy | Set retention; execution logging at `INFO` with data tracing is a large ingestion cost | CloudWatch Logs retention |\\n| SLS-APG-083 | COST | LOW | Stage with near-zero `Count` over the window that still holds a cache cluster or a custom domain | Decommission unused stages | API Gateway pricing |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Remediation snippets\\n\\n### Enable structured access logging on a stage\\n\\n```bash\\naws apigateway update-stage \\\\\\n  --rest-api-id abc123 \\\\\\n  --stage-name prod \\\\\\n  --patch-operations \\\\\\n    op=replace,path=/accessLogSettings/destinationArn,value=arn:aws:logs:REGION:ACCOUNT:log-group:/aws/apigateway/prod \\\\\\n Two of them are easy to get wrong, so scan\\nfor **all** the listed variants rather than the one you expect:\\n\\n| Pattern | What it indicates |\\n|---|---|\\n| `Status: timeout` (in the REPORT line) **or** `Task timed out` | invocation hit the configured timeout. Current managed runtimes record the timeout as a `Status: timeout` field on the REPORT line and may emit no `Task timed out` message at all \u2014 scan for both |\\n| `Runtime.OutOfMemory` / `Runtime exited` | the runtime process was killed for exceeding the memory allocation |\\n| `MemoryError` (Python) / `JavaScript heap out of memory` (Node.js) / `OutOfMemoryError` (Java) | the language runtime's allocator refused the allocation. Duration: 12.34 ms Billed Duration: 100 ms Memory Size: 128 MB Max Memory Used: 18 MB Init Duration: 250.00 ms Status: timeout`\\n- JSON (`LogFormat: JSON`) \u2014 read `record.metrics.maxMemoryUsedMB`, `record.metrics.memorySizeMB`,\\n  `record.metrics.initDurationMs`, `record.metrics.billedDurationMs`\\n\\nFrom the sampled REPORT lines compute peak `Max Memory Used`, memory utilization against\\n`MemorySize`, cold-start count as a share of invocations, and p99 `Init Duration`. The Lambda best\\npractices guide names `Max Memory Used` as the signal for over- and under-provisioning, and CloudWatch\\nrecommends alarming Lambda Insights `memory_utilization` at 90%.\\n\\n**`Max Memory Used` does not always reveal a memory failure.** When the language runtime's allocator\\nrefuses a large allocation up front \u2014 a Python `MemoryError`, for instance \u2014 the pages are never\\ntouched, so `Max Memory Used` can report a low figure on the very invocation that failed for lack of\\nmemory. Observed in practice: a 128 MB function that failed with `MemoryError` reported\\n`Max Memory Used: 35 MB`. Treat the log evidence as authoritative for memory failures and\\n`Max Memory Used` as the signal for right-sizing a *healthy* function.\\n\\nSample rather than scan exhaustively: 200\u2013500 REPORT lines spread across the window is enough to\\nsize memory, and keeps the log-read cost bounded.\\n\"}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_xMFayUBIBKWj9Ocsh28pe1", "content": "[{'text': '# API Quirks and Error Handling Reference\\n\\nHow to handle the errors a review will hit, and the API responses whose obvious reading is wrong.\\n\\n## Error Handling\\n\\n| Error | Cause | Resolution |\\n|-------|-------|-----------|\\n| `AccessDeniedException` / `AccessDenied` | the agent role lacks a read permission | skip that check, record it in Scope Covered, and list the missing action in the report |\\n| `NO_ELEVATED_ROLE_FOR_ACCOUNT` on an otherwise-permitted call | an agent-space policy restriction, not an IAM gap \u2014 observed on `lambda:GetFunctionEventInvokeConfig` | say so precisely in Scope Covered: the permission exists, the platform declined the call. ## Recommendations

Ordered by urgency. I made no changes; the commands below are for you to run.

**1. Within 24–48 hours: `slsreview-legacy-runtime`.** Move it off python3.9, confirm why every invocation fails, and add an OnFailure destination so dropped events are kept.
```bash
aws lambda update-function-configuration --function-name slsreview-legacy-runtime \
  --runtime python3.13 --architectures arm64
aws lambda put-function-event-invoke-config --function-name slsreview-legacy-runtime \
  --maximum-retry-attempts 2 --maximum-event-age-in-seconds 3600 \
  --destination-config '{"OnFailure":{"Destination":"arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:<acct>:<failure-queue>"}}'
```
Also move `DB_PASSWORD`, `API_KEY` and `SERVICE_TOKEN` to Secrets Manager.

**2. Within 24–48 hours: harden the stream mapping.** Take the UUID from `list-event-source-mappings`.
```bash
aws lambda update-event-source-mapping --uuid <uuid> \
  --maximum-retry-attempts 5 --maximum-record-age-in-seconds 3600 \
  --bisect-batch-on-function-error --function-response-types ReportBatchItemFailures \
  --destination-config '{"OnFailure":{"Destination":"arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:<acct>:<stream-failures>"}}'
```

**3. Within 1 week: the SQS queue and its consumer.** Raise the visibility timeout to 6 × 60 s, add a DLQ with maxReceiveCount of 5 or more, and enable partial batch response on the mapping. Raise the consumer's reserved concurrency to at least 5.
```bash
aws sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url <slsreview-no-dlq-queue-url> --attributes VisibilityTimeout=360
aws lambda update-event-source-mapping --uuid <uuid> --function-response-types ReportBatchItemFailures
```

**4. Within 1 week: the shared role.** Replace `far-too-broad` with actions and ARNs scoped to the real queues, table and topic.

**5. Within 1 week: async failure capture across the account.** Add OnFailure destinations to the 7 async functions, DLQs to the 6 rule targets and 2 schedules, and set a sensible MaximumEventAge on `exb-dispatcher-heartbeat`.
```yaml
Targets:
  - Id: Dispatcher
    Arn: !GetAtt DispatcherFunction.Arn
    DeadLetterConfig: { Arn: !GetAtt EventBridgeDLQ.Arn }
    RetryPolicy: { MaximumRetryAttempts: 10, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds: 3600 }
```

**6. Within 1 week: DynamoDB.** Enable PITR and deletion protection on the tables that hold data.
```bash
aws dynamodb update-continuous-backups --table-name example-tracker \
  --point-in-time-recovery-specification PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=true
aws dynamodb update-table --table-name example-tracker --deletion-protection-enabled
```

**7. Within 1 week: APIs.**
- On the HTTP API, add authorization on the routes (an IAM or JWT authorizer), stage throttling, and access logs.
- On REST `prod`, turn off data tracing, add access logs and ERROR-level logging, and enable tracing.
```bash
aws apigateway update-stage --rest-api-id <id> --stage-name prod --patch-operations \
  op=replace,path=/*/*/logging/dataTrace,value=false \
  op=replace,path=/*/*/logging/loglevel,value=ERROR \
  op=replace,path=/*/*/metrics/enabled,value=true
```

**8. Within 1 week: the state machine.** Add Retry (including the Lambda transient errors), Catch, TaskTimeout and a top-level timeout, plus logging and tracing.
```bash
aws stepfunctions update-state-machine --state-machine-arn <arn> \
  --tracing-configuration enabled=true \
```

## Recommendations

Ordered by urgency. I made no changes; the commands below are for you to run.

**1. Within 24–48 hours: `slsreview-legacy-runtime`.** Move it off python3.9, confirm why every invocation fails, and add an OnFailure destination so dropped events are kept.
```bash
aws lambda update-function-configuration --function-name slsreview-legacy-runtime \
  --runtime python3.13 --architectures arm64
aws lambda put-function-event-invoke-config --function-name slsreview-legacy-runtime \
  --maximum-retry-attempts 2 --maximum-event-age-in-seconds 3600 \
  --destination-config '{"OnFailure":{"Destination":"arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:<acct>:<failure-queue>"}}'
```
Also move `DB_PASSWORD`, `API_KEY` and `SERVICE_TOKEN` to Secrets Manager.

**2. Within 24–48 hours: harden the stream mapping.** Take the UUID from `list-event-source-mappings`.
```bash
aws lambda update-event-source-mapping --uuid <uuid> \
  --maximum-retry-attempts 5 --maximum-record-age-in-seconds 3600 \
  --bisect-batch-on-function-error --function-response-types ReportBatchItemFailures \
  --destination-config '{"OnFailure":{"Destination":"arn:aws:sqs:us-east-1:<acct>:<stream-failures>"}}'
```

**3. Within 1 week: the SQS queue and its consumer.** Raise the visibility timeout to 6 × 60 s, add a DLQ with maxReceiveCount of 5 or more, and enable partial batch response on the mapping. Raise the consumer's reserved concurrency to at least 5.
```bash
aws sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url <slsreview-no-dlq-queue-url> --attributes VisibilityTimeout=360
aws lambda update-event-source-mapping --uuid <uuid> --function-response-types ReportBatchItemFailures
```

**4. Within 1 week: the shared role.** Replace `far-too-broad` with actions and ARNs scoped to the real queues, table and topic.

**5. Within 1 week: async failure capture across the account.** Add OnFailure destinations to the 7 async functions, DLQs to the 6 rule targets and 2 schedules, and set a sensible MaximumEventAge on `exb-dispatcher-heartbeat`.
```yaml
Targets:
  - Id: Dispatcher
    Arn: !GetAtt DispatcherFunction.Arn
    DeadLetterConfig: { Arn: !GetAtt EventBridgeDLQ.Arn }
    RetryPolicy: { MaximumRetryAttempts: 10, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds: 3600 }
```

**6. Within 1 week: DynamoDB.** Enable PITR and deletion protection on the tables that hold data.
```bash
aws dynamodb update-continuous-backups --table-name example-tracker \
  --point-in-time-recovery-specification PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=true
aws dynamodb update-table --table-name example-tracker --deletion-protection-enabled
```

**7. Within 1 week: APIs.**
- On the HTTP API, add authorization on the routes (an IAM or JWT authorizer), stage throttling, and access logs.
- On REST `prod`, turn off data tracing, add access logs and ERROR-level logging, and enable tracing.
```bash
aws apigateway update-stage --rest-api-id <id> --stage-name prod --patch-operations \
  op=replace,path=/*/*/logging/dataTrace,value=false \
  op=replace,path=/*/*/logging/loglevel,value=ERROR \
  op=replace,path=/*/*/metrics/enabled,value=true
```

**8. Within 1 week: the state machine.** Add Retry (including the Lambda transient errors), Catch, TaskTimeout and a top-level timeout, plus logging and tracing.
```bash
aws stepfunctions update-state-machine --state-machine-arn <arn> \
```
